slides.text:
Horn clauses
A Horn clause is a disjunctive clause containing at most one positive
literal. A definite clause contains exactly one positive literal.
A Horn formula is a conjunction of Horn clauses.

slides.title: Horn SAT
slides.text:
Horn SAT
Horn SAT is the problem of deciding whether a finite conjunction
of Horn clauses is satisfiable.
Start from the facts.
Whenever all premises of a rule are known, add its conclusion.
If that makes a constraint’s premises true, derive 
⊥
: unsatisfiable.
Otherwise satisfiable: 1 for every derived atom, 0 for the rest.
Those atoms are true in every model, so this is the least model:
it makes no additional atom true.

slides.title: Planning by SAT solving
slides.text:
Planning by SAT solving
A fluent describes a feature of a world whose truth may
Instructions:
change over time. A separate atom represents its value
at each time point.
On(X, Y, t)
X is on Y at time t
Stack(X, Y, t)
put X on Y at time t
Unstack(X, Y, t)
take X off Y at time t
Initial state: 
On(G, R, 0)
Goal state: 
On(R, G, 2)
A model assigns a value to every state and action atom at every time point:
a full history. The plan is what its true action atoms say.

slides.title: What the KB has to say
slides.text:
What the KB has to say
How the world works:
¬On(X, X, t)
On(X, Y, t) → ¬On(Y, X, t)
What an action does:
Stack(X, Y, t) → On(X, Y, t+1)
Unstack(X, Y, t) → ¬On(X, Y, t+1)
When an action may be taken:
Unstack(X, Y, t) → On(X, Y, t)
You can only unstack blocks that are actually stacked.
Every one of these is a Horn clause: one positive literal in
disjunctive form. So far, the encoding is Horn.
